convoLines.text: "Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"We need to — Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Columbus, Ohio. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about ducks in a row last night — what to even CALL it. 'Don't-Look' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Anyway, that's me."
«Oui, oui, exactement.» (Yes, yes, exactly. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«Merci. Vraiment, merci.» (Thanks. Truly, thanks. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Je n'oublierai pas.» (I won't forget. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Tu as à manger ? Quelque chose ?» (Do you have food? Something? — you're fairly sure)
Ornella blinks. Then cracks up. "You said that BEAUTIFULLY. It means nothing like what you think it means." They teach you the right word, still laughing.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Still on who you don't trust."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? You know?"
"Have you heard what they're calling ducks in a row? Hank is pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About where you're from — Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"Still on where you're from."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Nicole is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
«Habari! Wewe... jina lako nani?»
«Ndiyo, ndiyo, hasa.» They nod back, slowly.
«Wewe ni mtu mwema.» (you catch 'mwema' — good) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Sitaisahau wema huu.» (you catch 'wema' — kindness) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Unaelewa?» (you catch 'Unaelewa' — understand)
Wanjiru laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Sahihi.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Somchai — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
«Salut ! Comment tu t'appelles ?» (Hi! What's your name? — you're fairly sure) "You good?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«D'accord.» (Agreed. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«T'es un amour, merci.» (You're a darling, thanks. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Tu es quelqu'un de bien.» (You're someone good. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Où est-ce qu'on dort, ici ?» (Where do we sleep, here? — you're fairly sure)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Somchai glances around first. "People are saying things. About you. Is any of it true?"
They nod. "Okay."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Halfway to the ridge, Somchai freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"Still on needing to be alone."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I be honest? Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Carl shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Oh." A long pause. "I didn't think it was anyone's. It's gone — I ate it days ago. I'm sorry."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on their secret."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
«C'est quoi, cet endroit ? Où sommes-nous ?» (What is this place? Where are we? — you're fairly sure)
«Exactement. T'as tout compris.» (Exactly. You've got it all. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.

"Right. Go on, then."

Ignorance got us here. Knowledge gets us out. Or it doesn't, but I'd rather know.

"BROTHERS! That's The Union Rep telling you it's about to move. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"The sky changed and nobody knows why. That is unacceptable to me personally."
"I need the mechanism. Not the story — the mechanism. Stories lie. Mechanisms don't."
"Still on what they want."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "The Blood Tithe. They just... took Ornella. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Je ne comprends rien. Rien !» (I don't understand anything. Nothing! — you're fairly sure) "Hello?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«C'est vrai.» (It's true. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«T'es un amour, merci.» (You're a darling, thanks. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Tu es quelqu'un de bien.» (You're someone good. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Ça fait combien de jours, ici ?» (How many days has it been, here? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
